correctness.rationale: Bandelt–Mulder pendant/true-twin/false-twin theorem makes both finite enumerations exhaustive for connected distance-hereditary graphs. Independent generation via complete atlas and constructive recurrence both recover 1484 order-eight types; every vertex is rooted and its refinement partition is compared with exact root-preserving isomorphism/orbits. Both find exactly two exceptions and the separate exact witness proof derives cell/orbit sizes 1,7 versus 1,3,4. Embedded code and replay outputs demonstrate complete checks. Scope only n<=8; no infinite inference.

value.rationale: The first exact failure cutoff for rooted two-variable counting types versus graph stabilizer orbits in a natural split-decomposable hereditary family is a motivated structural classification. It isolates exactly two minimal, inequivalent 8-vertex models and explains their unresolved cells by two distinct regular 7-vertex induced configurations. The finite result is sharp and its exhaustive boundary is mathematically natural, rather than an arbitrary subfamily slice.
